newsitem.title: USA: KCBT wheat ends mostly lower in light volume.
newsitem.headline: KCBT wheat ends mostly lower in light volume.

text.p: KCBT hard red winter wheat futures closed mostly lower in very light volume amid speculation farmers would resume wheat sales after the first of the year, traders said.
"There was just no volume," one trader said. "There was some anticipation of farmer selling right after the first of the year."
Some farmers had been storing wheat to defer tax payments until next year. They were expected to sell wheat in January.
Weakening cash bids in the country also contributed to the losses and supported ideas farmers planned to sell.
Basis bids were lower in parts of Kansas after Monday's heavy farmer sales filled pipelines. While selling was lighter on Tuesday, demand was also weak and most elevators were covered nearby.

Rumors Brazil was looking to buy 500,000 tonnes Argentine wheat for February/March delivery limited losses and news Pakistan was tendering for 270,000 tonnes U.S. or Australian wheat was also considered supportive.
Wheat closed three cents per bushel lower to 1/2 cent higher with March down 3 at $3.95-1/4. The exchange will be closed Wednesday in observance of the New Year's Day holiday.
